chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from the one who narrated it, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Muthanna al-Hannat, from Abu Baseer, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying regarding the woman performing Tamattu': if she enters the state of Ihram while pure, then menstruates before she completes her Tamattu', she performs Sa'ee but does not perform Tawaf until she becomes pure. Then she completes her Tawaf, and she has completed her Umrah. And if she entered Ihram while menstruating, she does not perform Sa'ee and does not perform Tawaf until she becomes pure.

key_terms.أَحْرَمَتْ: She entered the state of Ihram (ritual consecration)
key_terms.الْمَرْأَةِ الْمُتَمَتِّعَةِ: The woman performing Tamattu' (a type of Umrah combined with Hajj)
key_terms.سَعَتْ: She performed Sa'ee (the ritual walking between Safa and Marwah)
key_terms.طَوَافَهَا: Her Tawaf (ritual circumambulation of the Kaaba)

ai.seo_question: What are the ritual obligations for a woman performing Umrah if she menstruates during the pilgrimage rites?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the procedural nuances of Umrat al-Tamattu' for menstruating women, distinguishing between those who enter Ihram in a state of purity versus those already menstruating. It establishes that menstruation suspends the performance of rituals (Sa'ee and Tawaf) without invalidating the Umrah itself, requiring only the resumption upon achieving purity. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic view that major ritual impurity (hayd) acts as a temporary barrier to specific acts of worship rather than a nullifier of the pilgrimage contract.
